# wafer v1.1.4 - Table of Contents

> Wafer is an Elixir library to make writing drivers for i2c and SPI connected
peripherals and interacting with GPIO pins easier.

## Pages

- [Wafer](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/readme.md)
- [Change Log](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/changelog.md)

## Modules

- [Wafer](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.md): Welcome to Wafer. The funkiest way to write hardware drivers.
- [Wafer.Chip](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Chip.md): A `Chip` is a physical peripheral with registers which can be read from and
written to.
- [Wafer.Conn](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Conn.md): Defines a behaviour for connecting to a peripheral.
- [Wafer.DLL](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.DLL.md): Implements a safe bytewise data-link-layer which allows the transmission and
receiption of arbitrary erlang terms in tiny packets.
- [Wafer.DLL.Rx](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.DLL.Rx.md): Bytewise reception buffer for our data link layer.

- [Wafer.DLL.Tx](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.DLL.Tx.md): A bytewise transmission buffer for our data link layer.

- [Wafer.DeviceID](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.DeviceID.md): Allows devices to generate a unique identifier.
- [Wafer.Driver.Circuits.GPIO](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Driver.Circuits.GPIO.md): A connection to a native GPIO pin via Circuits' GPIO driver.
- [Wafer.Driver.Circuits.GPIO.Dispatcher](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Driver.Circuits.GPIO.Dispatcher.md): This module implements a simple dispatcher for GPIO interrupts when using
`Circuits.GPIO`.
- [Wafer.Driver.Circuits.I2C](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Driver.Circuits.I2C.md): A connection to a chip via Circuits' I2C driver.
- [Wafer.Driver.Circuits.SPI](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Driver.Circuits.SPI.md): A connection to a chip via Circuits's SPI driver.
- [Wafer.Driver.Fake](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Driver.Fake.md): This module provides a fake driver which you can use in your tests.
- [Wafer.Format](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Format.md): Handy functions for formatting bytes, especially for debugging.

- [Wafer.GPIO](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.GPIO.md): A `GPIO` is a physical pin which can be read from and written to.
- [Wafer.Guards](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Guards.md): Handy guards which you can use in your code to assert correct values.

- [Wafer.I2C](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.I2C.md): A protocol for interacting with I2C devices directly.  Most of the time you'll
want to use the `Chip` protocol for working with registers, but this is
provided for consistency's sake.
- [Wafer.InterruptRegistry](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.InterruptRegistry.md): This module provides Wafer's interrupt registry.  This allows multiple
subscribers to be subscribed to interrupts from many different pins.
- [Wafer.Registers](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Registers.md): This module provides helpful macros for specifying the registers used to
communicate with your device.
- [Wafer.Release](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Release.md): A protocol for releasing connections.  The opposite of `Conn`'s `acquire/1`.
- [Wafer.SPI](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.SPI.md): A (very simple) protocol for interacting with SPI connected devices.
- [Wafer.Twiddles](https://wafer.hexdocs.pm/Wafer.Twiddles.md): Handy functions for dealing with bits and bytes in the wild.
